site.name: Cameron Wansing
site.headline: I build AI tools for the places I spend my time: work, church, and my own to-do list.
site.intro: I'm a college student near Kansas City working toward a career in finance. At ProAthlete, the company behind JustBats and JustGloves, I put AI to work across departments. These are a few things I've built, with what each one does and how I got there.
offClock: On the golf course most afternoons
Leveling a character in World of Warcraft
site.footer: Built and maintained by Cameron Wansing.

projects.title: ProAthlete SiteWatch
projects.oneLiner: Scans ProAthlete's online stores and gives the team one list of typos, broken links and page problems to fix.
projects.summary: SiteWatch reads through ProAthlete's storefront pages and collects what it finds wrong into one place. Each issue has a severity, the pages it affects, and a plain-language explanation of what to change, so someone who has never seen the scan can open it and start fixing.
projects.why: Small mistakes on product pages are easy to miss and hard to keep track of across a large store. I wanted the team to have one current list of what needs fixing instead of finding problems one at a time.

process.title: Crawl the sites
process.text: A scanner crawls the store pages and records what each page contains, including its links and images.

process.title: Find and rank the issues
process.text: Findings are grouped into issues and ranked from critical to informational, so the most damaging problems sit at the top.

process.title: Check the results by hand
process.text: Before sharing anything, I reviewed flagged links and images myself. A list like this only helps if people trust what is on it.

process.title: Explain each issue
process.text: Every issue shows where it appears and what to do about it, written for the person fixing the page and not for the person who built the scanner.

process.title: Share it with the team
process.text: The results are published as a read-only site behind a shared password, with a dashboard, an issue list and a monitoring view.

projects.learned: Finding problems was the easy half. The work that mattered was making the results trustworthy and clear enough that other people would act on them.
projects.status: Deployed for the ProAthlete team. The live tool is private to the company, and scan results are not shown here.

projects.title: Zion BibleGraph
projects.oneLiner: Turns my church's sermons into a searchable library of summaries, topics and Bible passages.
projects.summary: Zion BibleGraph is a public site where anyone at my church can revisit a sermon, read a clear summary, follow a topic across messages, or see every sermon that used a given Bible passage. Topics link to the passages used to teach them, with the sermon evidence behind each connection.
projects.why: I had two years of sermon and Bible study notes that were hard to search, revisit or share. It started as a personal notes vault, and I turned it into a site so other people could use it too.

process.title: Pull in the sermons
process.text: The pipeline reads the church's public podcast feed and downloads each new message.

process.title: Transcribe the audio
process.text: Each recording is split into segments and transcribed with an AI speech model. I compare segment coverage against the length of the original recording.

process.title: Summarize and connect
process.text: AI drafts a summary and pulls out the topics, speakers, series and Bible references. Quotations in each summary are checked against the transcript.

process.title: Publish as linked pages
process.text: Every sermon, topic, passage, speaker and series becomes its own page, linked to the others and published as a static site.

process.title: Verify before it goes live
process.text: Automated tests and a link check run before each update, so a new batch of sermons can't quietly break the library.

projects.learned: AI projects are strongest when they help a real community reach something valuable. I also learned to label AI-assisted summaries honestly and point people back to the original message.
projects.status: Live and public, with new sermons added in batches.

projects.title: Questline
projects.kind: Mac app for tasks and time
projects.oneLiner: A Mac task manager that turns my projects into quests, styled after World of Warcraft's quest log.
projects.summary: Questline is a native Mac app for projects, tasks and time. Each project is broken into steps, and a small tracker window floats on the desktop showing the three or four quests I can start right now. It times the work, compares my estimates with what happened, and plans the day around my calendar with room left for leisure and open time.
projects.why: Between school, work, my resale businesses and church, I have a lot of projects running at once. I play World of Warcraft, and I wanted my real work to feel like its quest log: a short list of things I can start right now.

process.title: Write the full spec first
process.text: I started with a long written description of how the app should behave, including what it should never do, such as punishing scores or writing to calendars it doesn't own.

process.title: Explore four visual directions
process.text: I generated four design concepts and kept all of them as selectable themes. Parchment Quest Log, the Warcraft-inspired one, is the default.

process.title: Build in increments with an AI coding agent
process.text: The app was built one slice at a time in Swift, each with its own tests and a written record of what was verified and what was still open.

process.title: Connect Google Calendar carefully
process.text: It reads my personal, school and work calendars but only writes to one calendar it created. I verified that with a real create, move and delete round trip.

process.title: Use it every day
process.text: I run my own days in it, and each rough edge I hit becomes the next change, like pasting a numbered list to add a whole project's steps at once.

projects.learned: Writing down exactly what I wanted, and what counted as done, mattered more than any single prompt. The honest verification notes kept me from believing something worked before it did.
projects.status: Installed and in daily use on my Mac. It is a personal app and is not distributed.
